# CEREMO instructions

Access policy, approved 5 November 2026: anonymous visitors may read catalogues and limited provider summaries. Full profiles, detailed reviews and contact destinations require an authenticated, registered ACTIVE account, using the existing account check. Private tenant access additionally requires database-authoritative accepted membership and the operation's owner/role permission; registration or ROLE_ADMIN alone grants no general tenant read. Follow [ADR 11.10](../docs/03-technical-requirements.md#1110-registered-profile-and-contact-access). Older unconditional public-profile/contact guidance is superseded. Account gates do not constitute marketing consent.

Mandatory JaCoCo rule: require 100% line and 100% branch coverage per application class from combined regular/PostgreSQL test data. Enforce `CLASS` rules with `LINE`/`BRANCH`, `MISSEDCOUNT` and a maximum of zero. Never lower/bypass the gate, add exclusions/annotations or use assertion-free tests to manufacture a pass. Inspect uncovered behaviour and test it meaningfully. A passing test run below 100% is a failed coverage checkpoint. The user's Salesync permission on 21 October 2026 applies only to this coverage-rule reference, not future unrelated work.

Read the [research memory index](research/README.md) before deep research or coding, then load only the relevant domain, application, repository, controller, ports/adapters, database or quality entries. Save each deep investigation in its matching category using the [entry template](research/entry-template.md), update the index and verification status, and cross-link related layers. Recheck current source and version-sensitive evidence; cached research is not proof of implementation. Keep this memory outside the eight-file `docs/` set.

Before coding guidance, implementation or review, read the persistent [security and quality rules](security-quality-rules.md) and [AGENTS.md security instructions](../AGENTS.md#security-and-quality-before-every-coding-step). Apply the relevant controls and negative tests to the current change. Recheck installed SonarQube/JaCoCo tooling before giving commands or claiming results; never expose tokens or bypass findings to get a passing gate.

Do not consult or use Salesync for code, ideas, evidence, architecture or writing references unless the user explicitly requests it for the current task. Earlier copying permissions are not continuing permission. Inspect and reuse existing CEREMO code normally. Prioritise established, highly starred maintainer repositories, official Spring sources and verified company engineering publications. Research attributable public Medium, LinkedIn and Slack material when relevant, and verify implementation claims against source/tests. Attach exact source links, short evidence excerpts, adaptations and checks to every coding guide; follow [research rules](../AGENTS.md#research-before-recommendations).

Write short explanations, familiar business terms, numbered requirements and concrete implementation tasks. Read [the writing and naming guide](../AGENTS.md#writing-and-naming).

For investor/CTO functional specifications, follow [the approved functional-writing rules](../AGENTS.md#functional-specifications-for-investors-and-ctos) and [their research record](research/application/customer-lifecycle.md#professional-specification-method-and-rewrite-4-november-2026). Use numbered business modules with Function / Required behaviour / Essential business rule tables. Cover the complete customer cycle and supporting provider/staff operations. Keep detailed implementation/testing checks in developer documentation and preserve an internal coverage mapping when consolidating. Do not restore the removed introduction, permissions matrix or diagram. Distinguish proposed/later scope, retain unapproved decisions and record Grammarly as pending until actually checked. Use installed skills; no external specification skill was installed by this review.

- Current implementation work is on the backend. Frontend stack: Next.js (React), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query, and React Hook Form with Zod. Unspecified visual, hosting and integration decisions remain `null`; see [the frontend brief](../docs/05-ui-ux-design-brief.md).
- Greater Accra first; all occasions and festivals; provider subscriptions only. Customers browse free; provider listings have a trial, then an optional paid subscription. Outside conversations and service payments are permitted. No booking commission or customer service checkout in the MVP; see [ADR 0006](../docs/03-technical-requirements.md#116-provider-subscriptions-and-discovery).
- Payment cannot buy verification success, favourable reviews or an undisclosed ranking. Label sponsored placement; support optional/editable customer preferences and relevant new providers without invented stars.
- Java 25, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL and Gradle. Keycloak in development and production. SonarQube and JaCoCo for development/CI.
- Use strict DDD with ports and adapters inside feature packages such as `providermanagement`, `discovery` and `enquirymanagement`. Follow [architecture rules](../AGENTS.md#architecture-ddd-with-ports-and-adapters): plain Java domain/application core, domain repository contracts, explicit application inbound/outbound ports, HTTP and persistence adapters, and outer Spring wiring/transaction boundaries. Teach Domain -> Repository contracts -> Application -> Controllers. Keep JPA entities separate; controllers call inbound ports, never repositories.
- Prefer names such as `ProviderService`, `ProviderResource`, `RestCreateProviderRequest` and `ProviderJpaEntity`. Keep application methods direct: `create(...)`, `findById(id)`, `acknowledge(enquiryId)`.
- Use standard REST paths: `/api/v1/providers`, `/api/v1/events`, `/api/v1/enquiries`, `/api/v1/payments`.
- Explain who does what and what happens when it fails. Remove hype, repeated caveats, artificial labels and commentary about writing the document.
- Preserve facts, source links, amounts, security checks and payment rules. Keep future features separate from implemented behaviour. Do not invent experience, authorship, customer evidence or business results.
- Keep exactly eight numbered files (01–08) in `docs/`. Fold research into document 01 and architecture decisions/history into document 03; keep writing/method guidance in `AGENTS.md`. Do not create separate reports, ADRs or a docs README unless requested.
- Approved exception, 4 November 2026: retain 01–08 and the separately requested [09-functional-requirements.md](../docs/09-functional-requirements.md). Nine files are now authorised; older eight-file counts in cached context are superseded. Additional documents still need approval.
- Further approved exception, 4 November 2026: the local private `docs/startup doc/startup docs.md` is permitted in addition to the nine numbered files. It is Git-ignored; do not force-add, publish, upload or copy its contents elsewhere without explicit approval. Keep detailed startup research/evidence there, with only a local pointer in the research index. Ten files may exist locally; the nine numbered documents remain the shared product baseline. Ignoring is not encryption/access control.
- Task-list exception, 4 November 2026: `docs/startup doc/tasklist.md` is the private execution record for the founder guide. Eleven local documentation files are authorised; the shared baseline remains nine numbered documents. Keep the task list Git-ignored and do not publish or transfer it without approval. Update task status there and retain research/rationale in the guide.
- Match related documents when changing names. Do not rename existing source code unless the task requires it.

Further project context: [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), [documentation](../README.md#documentation).

5 November 2026 consolidation: use the single `account` module for local users, registration/activation, identity mapping and account/staff checks. `usermanagement` is removed. Use `wire/account/AccountConfiguration`; follow [ADR 11.9](../docs/03-technical-requirements.md#119-consolidate-the-account-module). Historical names in research are not current package instructions. API/database contracts remain unchanged.

Before every backend guide, snippet, implementation or code review, check both the [shared package reuse map](shared-package-map.md) and [wire package reuse map](wire-package-map.md), then read current source, callers, properties and tests. As of 5 November 2026, shared has 88 Java files in 12 packages; wire has 16 files in nine areas and eight dedicated test classes plus the OIDC fixture/full-stack security checks. Refresh the maps when behaviour changes. Provider businesses now use the approved `tenant` module; customers remain independent. Membership is database-authoritative; the inherited token-organisation filter stays off. Workspace status, publication, verification and subscription are separate. See [implementation evidence](research/ports-and-adapters/provider-account-security.md).

Apply the [readable Java workflow](skills/ceremo-shared-wire/SKILL.md#write-readable-source-backed-java): exact maintainer references/tests, explicit constructors and business operations, existing names, narrow changes and no unnecessary layers or Lombok. Distinguish copied/adapted mechanisms from original CEREMO policy. A humanizer or persona cannot establish code correctness. On 4 November 2026 the user approved activation only from trusted boolean Keycloak `email_verified=true`; registration otherwise stays PENDING, later activation is explicit, reads never activate, and restricted accounts cannot self-reactivate. Verification grants no provider/staff/billing privileges.

Apply the project-local [CEREMO shared/wire reuse skill](skills/ceremo-shared-wire/SKILL.md). This explicit link is required context even if the extension does not discover skills automatically. Reuse suitable shared helpers and wire beans/configuration whenever needed, without forcing dependencies on unrelated features. Keep Spring/JPA/wire out of the plain domain/application core. Check bean conditions, property precedence, visibility and complete use-case transactions; do not recreate existing executors, CORS, auditing, cache or OpenAPI configuration. Each guide needs a brief reuse note: shared reused; wire reused or why unnecessary; new code/gap; verification.

Mandatory before any code or guide: after research, inspect the actual current feature, `shared`, `wire` and relevant tests for reusable behaviour. Follow the [reuse check](../AGENTS.md#mandatory-reuse-check-before-code-or-guides). Prefer suitable existing implementations, cite the files/methods being reused, and explain the gap before proposing anything new. Preserve DDD dependency boundaries; do not duplicate utilities, validation, authentication or error handling already available.

The user writes the application code. Follow [guided development](../AGENTS.md#guided-development-the-user-writes-the-code): research actual relevant Spring Boot classes and tests before each guide; cite source files and explain adaptations; teach package structure, methods, rules and checks in manageable steps. Do not edit application code/configuration unless explicitly asked. No Lombok dependencies or annotations; use explicit Java constructors/accessors or suitable records. Assess reference quality through maintainership, tests, maintenance, licence and compatibility; never invent author credentials or "100X" claims.

Before answering each prompt, follow [research before recommendations](../AGENTS.md#research-before-recommendations): investigate the current stage, demonstrate relevant behaviour in existing applications with primary sources, and inspect existing local/public code for learning or reuse. Explain the business workflow first. Distinguish evidence from proposals; check licences and compatibility before copying code, and state evidence gaps plainly.
